element.name: TCountdownEvent
element.short: Lightweight synchronization primitive that unblocks waiting threads when its signal count reaches zero.

descr.p: TCountdownEvent is a synchronization primitive for fork-join and dynamic task graphs where the number of subtasks may change dynamically during execution.

Unlike a manual counter combined with TCriticalSection and TEvent, TCountdownEvent uses lock-free atomic decrements on its fast path and only interacts with the underlying TSimpleEvent when transitioning between zero and non-zero counts.

element.name: TCountdownEvent.Create
element.short: Creates a countdown event with the specified initial count.

descr.p: Initializes CurrentCount and InitialCount to aInitialCount. If aInitialCount is 0, the event is created in the signaled state (IsSet = True). Raises ESyncObjectException if aInitialCount < 0.

element.name: TCountdownEvent.Signal
element.short: Decrements the current count by aSignalCount and signals waiting threads if the count reaches zero.

descr.p: Returns True if this call caused CurrentCount to transition to zero; returns False otherwise. Raises ESyncObjectException if aSignalCount <= 0 or if decrementing would make the count negative.
Raises ESyncObjectException if the event is already set (CurrentCount = 0) or if aSignalCount <= 0.

element.name: TCountdownEvent.TryAddCount
element.short: Attempts to increment CurrentCount if the event is not yet set.

descr.p: Returns True if CurrentCount was greater than zero and successfully incremented; returns False if the countdown has already reached zero.

element.name: TCountdownEvent.Reset
element.short: Resets CurrentCount and InitialCount to the specified value (or to InitialCount).

element.name: TCountdownEvent.WaitFor
element.short: Blocks the calling thread until CurrentCount reaches zero or the timeout expires.

element.name: TBarrier
element.short: Cyclic multi-phase barrier that synchronizes a group of threads at the end of each phase.

descr.p: TBarrier enables multiple threads (participants) to work concurrently on iterative algorithms (such as stencil computations, matrix solvers, or graph algorithms) through a series of phases.

Each participant calls SignalAndWait upon completing its work for the current phase. When the last participant arrives, the optional TBarrierPhaseAction callback is executed by that thread before all participants are released into the next phase. Internally, TBarrier uses dual ping-pong events (FPhaseEvents[0..1]) indexed by phase parity to avoid race conditions between fast threads entering phase P+1 and slow threads waking from phase P.

element.name: EBarrierPostPhaseException
element.short: Exception raised in all participating threads if the barrier's post-phase action raises an exception.

element.name: TSlimReaderWriterLock
element.short: Fast user-space reader/writer lock with lock-free atomic fast paths and writer-preference anti-starvation.

descr.p: TSlimReaderWriterLock allows multiple concurrent readers or a single exclusive writer. Uncontended acquisitions and releases execute purely in user space via atomic compare-and-swap (TryAcquireReadFast, TryAcquireWriteFast) and adaptive spinning (TSpinWait), falling back to kernel events only under contention.
Waiting writers set the FWaitingWriters counter, which prevents new readers from acquiring the lock and starving writers.

element.name: TSlimReadLockGuard
element.short: Managed record RAII guard for automatic BeginRead / EndRead on TSlimReaderWriterLock.

element.name: TSlimWriteLockGuard
element.short: Managed record RAII guard for automatic BeginWrite / EndWrite on TSlimReaderWriterLock.

element.name: TChannel
element.short: Thread-safe generic CSP channel supporting bounded and unbounded capacities, closing, and for..in iteration.

descr.p: TChannel<T> implements Go-style Communicating Sequential Processes (CSP) message passing between producer and consumer threads.

When created with aCapacity = 0, the channel is unbounded and grows its internal circular buffer dynamically. When created with aCapacity > 0, the channel is bounded and applies backpressure by blocking Send when the buffer is full.

Calling Close marks the channel as closed and wakes all waiting senders and receivers. Receivers can still drain any buffered items before Receive(out Item) returns False and for Msg in Channel do terminates cleanly.

element.name: EChannelClosedException
element.short: Exception raised when Send is called on a closed channel or Receive is called on a closed and empty channel.
